fields.meta_description: Build a website design questionnaire that turns a client's answers into a sitemap and a draft quote before the first call. Free to start.
fields.h1: Build a Website Design Questionnaire That Scopes the Site
fields.hero_description: Describe the sites you build and what you need to know before you quote. Emergent builds the website design questionnaire and keeps every client's answers in a database you own.
fields.features_heading: Where the Client's Answers Go Next
fields.features_subheading: A questionnaire pays off when its answers move the project forward. These six pieces carry them from the form into the plan.
fields.feature_1:
Page lists that become a sitemap

Give clients a list of common pages to tick, plus a box for anything missing. The ticked pages turn into a draft sitemap your team can reorder before the first design call.
fields.feature_2:
Reference sites with a reason attached

Ask for two or three sites the client admires, each with a link and one line on why. Make that line required, since a bare link says little about what the client wants copied.
fields.feature_3:
Content status for every page

Ask who supplies the words and images for each page and whether they exist yet. Every page still waiting on content shows up in the project plan as writing or photo work to schedule.
fields.feature_4:
Brand files uploaded with the answers

Collect the logo files and the brand guide as uploads on the same form. Each file is saved with the client's record instead of sitting in an email thread from three months ago.
fields.feature_5:
Reminders for half-finished answers

Email the client when the questionnaire sits half done past the delay you choose. The reminder names the sections still blank and stops as soon as the client submits the form.
fields.feature_6:
The whole questionnaire app in your repo

Export the codebase to GitHub on paid plans whenever you want it. A developer can add a proposal page or a client login later, and past answers stay in the database they started in.

fields.usecase_heading: What the Answers Decided on Four Projects
fields.tab_content_1:
Eight ticked pages, one sitemap and a $2,800 quote

Rowan Ellis designs sites for therapists at $350 a page. Her questionnaire lists 12 common pages with a box beside each. Cole Therapy ticks eight of them, including Book a Session. Those eight pages become the draft sitemap, and a draft quote of $2,800 reaches Rowan before the first call.
fields.tab_content_2:
Each retired URL mapped to its new page

Brightline Studio is rebuilding the site for Juniper Dental Group, which has 14 pages today. The questionnaire asks the office manager to mark each old URL keep or retire. Nine pages are kept. The five retired URLs each get a 301 redirect row naming the new page their visitors should land on.
fields.tab_content_3:
Past 500 products, the catalog comes in by CSV

Linden Tea Co sells loose-leaf tea and is moving its shop to Shopify. On the questionnaire, the owner enters 640 products. Any answer over 500 sends her Shopify's sample product CSV with a due date. The project plan then swaps manual product entry for a single import task.
fields.tab_content_4:
When board members disagree on style, the call starts there

Three board members at Maple Street Players fill in the same questionnaire for the theater's new site. Two describe the look they want as warm and playful. The treasurer picks formal. That split goes to the top of the discovery call agenda, with each person's reference sites beside their answer.

fields.howto_title: How to Write a Website Design Questionnaire
fields.howto_description: Decide what the answers must settle before you write the first question.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Start with the decisions it must settle
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Turn the page list into checkboxes
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Give style words, not a blank box
fields.howto_step_1_des: List the decisions you need made before you can quote: which pages, what budget, who supplies the content, and when the site must launch. Every question should feed one of them. Anything that does not can wait for the discovery call.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Open with what the business sells, who buys from it and what a visitor should do on the site, such as booking a visit or placing an order. Style questions get better answers once the client has pictured the customer the site is for.
fields.howto_step_3_des: List the pages sites in the client's field usually need and let them tick each one, with a free-text box for extras. A ticked list is quicker to answer than an open question, and it becomes your first sitemap without any retyping.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Give the client pairs of words to choose between, such as warm or formal and bold or quiet. Pairs are easier to answer than an empty style box. When several people at one client answer, any split between them shows up at once.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Ask who supplies copy and photos
fields.howto_step_5_des: For each page, ask whether the client has the words and images ready or needs them written and shot. A page-by-page answer shows what still has to be produced before you commit to a launch date in the proposal.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Set a budget floor before you send it
fields.howto_step_6_des: Ask for a budget range instead of an exact figure, and decide your minimum in advance. A client below it gets a short, kind reply pointing to a template or a peer. That saves both sides a call that cannot end in a project.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Test it on a phone before sending
fields.howto_step_7_des: Open the link on a phone and answer as a hurried client would, skipping every optional box. Check that the sitemap and the quote come out right. Then send it with the date you need it back, a few days before the discovery call.

plan.angle: The live top 10 is designers' own questionnaires as PDFs and web pages (Squarespace-hosted PDF, Rob Cubbon, EllinasDesign, Liz Kalloch, a 72-question list on BonFX) plus a Scribd copy and a Pinterest board. Every one stops at the list of questions. This page treats the questionnaire as the first working document of the site: the page list becomes a sitemap and a draft quote, a redesign's old URLs become a redirect sheet, a store's product count picks the import method, and a board's clashing style answers surface before the discovery call. The FAQ answers the People Also Ask questions on what to ask, what every site needs and the web design process.
